clue.text: See 10 across
Continue with one's own domestic animals, rearing 50%

definitions.note: to keep step is to continue marching in time

parts.note: to own something is to keep it, as in keeping a dog

indicators.note: rearing up, in a down entry, means the word for the animals is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: household animals are pets

explanation.surface: Someone carries on with their own pets, bringing up half of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' turns PETS into STEP; '50%' refers to that half of the answer being turned, the other half, KEEP, reading forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep step is to stay in time with marching companions, so it means to carry on alongside them.

clue.text: Sphere of Caesarean section

indicators.note: a section of the word Caesarean is just a slice of its letters, the run in its middle

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding question about the field to which a Caesarean belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' looks like part of 'Caesarean section', the operation, but it signals a slice of the word Caesarean.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere of activity is a field or region of interest, a common synonym.

clue.text: Bandleader's failure to secure any points

definitions.meaning: A famous British big-band leader; the 's stands for 'is'
a defeat in a league match earns a team no points

explanation.surface: A band's leader blows a contest without scoring a single point.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Loss led a popular British dance band from the 1930s to the 1980s; read 'Bandleader's' as 'the bandleader is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeat in football gives a team nothing in the league table, while Joe Loss is the bandleader's surname.

clue.text: Mad announcer of Alpine Time?

definitions.meaning: crazy or barmy in informal speech
the bird popping out of a Swiss clock calls each hour

explanation.surface: A crazed figure who proclaims the time in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: The Swiss cuckoo clock has a little bird that calls the hours, hence an announcer of Alpine time.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone crazy is nuts or loopy; and the bird in a Swiss clock calls the hour.

clue.text: Recently stolen jumper secreted in timber-built apartment 17? Unlikely

parts.note: stolen goods still easy to trace are called hot

indicators.note: hidden inside, so the jumper's letters are tucked within the timber

parts.note: elm is a timber used for building
a kangaroo jumps, and a roo is its short name

explanation.surface: A burglar hides a stolen pullover in a wooden flat, though the room number makes that doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a pullover but is the kangaroo. 17 is THIRTEEN, and many hotels skip room 13 for superstition, hence 'Unlikely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel's numbered rooms are apartments for guests, and room thirteen is often omitted out of superstition.

clue.text: Wetherspoon's unspoilt clubs anticipating a brawl, admitting posh 19 supper guest 17

indicators.note: coming before, so the clubs letter precedes the brawl
letting in, so the pub's initials take the posh letter inside them

parts.note: J D Wetherspoon is a chain of British pubs, abbreviated JD
U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U
sold 'as is' means in its original state
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a riot is a violent brawl

explanation.surface: A pub chain's clubbers gear up for a fight before letting in someone posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is LAST and 17 is THIRTEEN: at the Last Supper Judas was the thirteenth person at table. JD Wetherspoon is a British pub chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The disciple who betrayed Christ was one of the thirteen at the Last Supper, the guest whose presence made the table unlucky.

clue.text: Force into having relations — endless amusement on a cold evening!

indicators.note: goes into, so the force word sits within the trimmed relations word
the relations word loses its final letter

parts.note: akin means related, having family ties
to press someone is to force them

explanation.surface: Someone is forced into an affair, cast as endless fun on a chilly night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having relations' hints at sex but means being related; 'endless' leaves AKI, and 'into' sets the force word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The socialising after a day's skiing is evening entertainment in snowy resorts, so cold-evening fun.

clue.text: End of arm set in plaster cast, 21 the 17th our downfall

indicators.note: fixed inside, so that letter is put among the letters of plaster
thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of the word arm

explanation.surface: A broken arm is set in a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is FRIDAY and 17 THIRTEEN: the Knights Templar were arrested on Friday 13 October 1307. 'cast' looks like the plaster cast but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The military order of knights was rounded up on a Friday the thirteenth, the start of its destruction.

clue.text: Fred Goodwin and co are asleep — pension's finally misplaced 17

indicators.note: put in the wrong place, so that letter shifts to another spot

parts.note: Fred Goodwin ran the Royal Bank of Scotland, so he and his colleagues are bankers
doze means sleep lightly

indicators.note: the last letter of the word pension

explanation.surface: Disgraced bank bosses nod off while a pension goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is THIRTEEN. Fred Goodwin was the RBS chief whose pension caused outrage after the 2008 crash; 'misplaced' sends the pension's N to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers traditionally gave thirteen loaves for twelve to avoid being fined for short weight.

clue.text: It's a bore, prosecutor breaking up fisticuffs

indicators.note: breaking into, so the prosecutor sits inside the fight word

parts.note: a brawl is a fist fight
DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A dull lawyer tries to stop a punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' suggests a tedious person; it is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: This tool makes small holes in wood, so it is literally something that bores.

clue.text: Miss lunch today? Ruefully, she will — so it requires rescheduling

definitions.text: Miss lunch today? Ruefully, she will

indicators.note: needs rearranging, so these letters must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Skipping lunch today with regret means rearranging the diary.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter's song 'Miss Otis Regrets' says she is unable to lunch today.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cole Porter's song the lady regrets she cannot come to lunch, so she misses it ruefully.

clue.text: The magic of the church that I didn't mean to suppress

indicators.note: hold down within, so the apology contains the church

parts.note: an apology, said as 'sorry'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An apologetic churchman hushes up some sorcery he did by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Witchcraft and wizardry are magic, the arts of spells and enchantment.

clue.text: French writer with a very poor green eye

parts.note: je is French for I, the person writing
lousy means very bad

explanation.surface: A French author has a bad squint in one green eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French writer' suggests a Frenchman with a pen; it is the French for 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is called the green-eyed monster, so the green eye is the envious feeling.

clue.text: Appropriately-numbered golden retriever plunging into the appropriate water

definitions.meaning: the Greek hero who fetched the Golden Fleece, here in a light numbered 13
the killer of the Friday the 13th films, who drowned in the camp lake

explanation.surface: A golden retriever with a fitting number jumps into the right water.
explanation.walkthrough: The light is 13 down, so the number fits. The golden retriever is not a dog: it is the Argonaut leader. The water is CAMP CRYSTAL LAKE (15 across).
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts' leader recovered the Golden Fleece, and the horror villain drowned as a boy in the camp's lake.

clue.text: It's done in fish collector

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
'there!' is said on finishing a task

explanation.surface: Someone collects something already finished inside a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gathers things up is a collector, as with a hunter-forager.

clue.text: Repack! All my acts murderous (in 21 the 17th)

indicators.note: savage, so these letters are hacked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cry to pack up after a series of killings.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is FRIDAY, 17 THIRTEEN: the summer camp is where the Friday the 13th horror films are set.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional summer camp where the slasher films take place, the setting of the Friday the 13th series.

clue.text: Inspector Doyle introduced in case that's variously read

parts.note: lest means for fear that

indicators.note: in different ways, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Introducing a detective in a case read in many ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doyle introduced' means the inspector Arthur Conan Doyle brought into the Sherlock Holmes stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scotland Yard detective of the Sherlock Holmes stories was a character created by Conan Doyle.

clue.text: Neither temperature would get you in here, in two ways — that is unfortunate

indicators.note: would produce by shuffling, so the letters are rearranged to give the number

explanation.surface: Neither temperature would let you in here; that's a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a second route, 'in two ways': two Ts with IN HERE rearranged give the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is considered unlucky, so it is the figure that brings misfortune.

clue.text: Flintstone's head drops, finding one rook in tree

clue.text: See out model, on foot

clue.text: 17 purveyors of 12 attempt to flee Midlands city

parts.note: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands
a try is an attempt

clue.text: Defoe's Man for all Seasons? 17 of me in each case

definitions.meaning: Robinson Crusoe's servant, there with him through every season

clue.text: See 7

indicators.note: the opening letter of orgies

clue.text: Die to get a couple to apres-ski?

explanation.definitionFit: A dice is a six-faced solid, and raising two to the third power gives the light number eight.

clue.text: See 25
The original unfed bird's in for it — this 21 snack her downfall

indicators.note: placed inside, so the shuffled letters go within the other words
inventive, novel, so these letters are given a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of unfed bird, the 's being 'is'

explanation.surface: The first woman, a hungry bird, is in trouble for eating something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The original bird' is Eve, the first woman, whose snack in Eden was her downfall. 21 is FRIDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The apple Eve ate in Eden was forbidden, and eating it was her ruin.
